definitions.explanation: Something that should definitely be read. Used to recommend books, articles, or other texts as essential or highly worthwhile.

examples.japanese: この{本|ほん}は{必読|ひつどく}だ。
{日本|にほん}の{歴史|れきし}に{興味|きょうみ}がある{人|ひと}には{必読|ひつどく}の{一冊|いっさつ}です。
examples.english: It's a must-read for anyone interested in Japanese history.

examples.japanese: {新入|しんにゅう}{社員|しゃいん}には、まずこの{社内|しゃない}マニュアルを{必読|ひつどく}{書|しょ}として{配|くば}っている。
examples.english: We distribute this internal manual to new employees as required reading.

notes:
Combines {必|ひつ} (must/necessarily) and {読|どく} (read), literally meaning "must read." Functions primarily as a noun modifier, often appearing before {書|しょ} (book) or {本|ほん}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {必読|ひつどく}{書|しょ}: must-read book
- {必読|ひつどく}の{一冊|いっさつ}: a must-read volume
- {必読|ひつどく}{文献|ぶんけん}: required reading (academic)
- {必読|ひつどく}リスト: required reading list

COMPOUNDS:
The {必|ひつ}〜 pattern appears in many similar compounds meaning "must-X":
- {必見|ひっけん}: must-see
- {必修|ひっしゅう}: required (course/subject)
- {必携|ひっけい}: must-have; indispensable

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {推薦|すいせん}{図書|としょ}: recommended book — a suggestion rather than a strong imperative
- {課題|かだい}{図書|としょ}: assigned reading — specifically assigned by a teacher or institution, not a general recommendation
